PlanOmics · bulk RNA-seq module

How a design moves through PlanOmics

A researcher answers questions one step at a time. Each answer updates the design state, the rulebook re-evaluates it, and the backend chooses what to ask next. The LLM only handles wording.

37 rules 28 golden scenarios 3 block · 10 strong · 9 suggest · 15 info 2 request a consult

Severity levels

infoContext for the researcher; nothing to change.
suggestA recommended default; easy to override.
strongStrongly recommended for this design; override only with a reason.
blockExport is blocked until resolved or a consult is requested.
consultRoutes the design to the Bioinformatics team without blocking.

Rules at each step

Each rule is listed at the first step where all of its trigger fields are known. What it recommends may land in a later step: depth rules triggered by the question fill in Sequencing.

1

Question

What is the biological question? Gene-level DE, isoforms, lncRNA; is global transcription expected to shift?

  • rnaseq.depth.isoformstrongteam
    When question.goal ∈ {isoform, splicing, fusion}
    Recommends
    • sequencing.target_reads_per_sample → 60M
    • sequencing.paired_end → yes
    Why does this matter?

    Isoform/splicing/fusion analyses need paired-end reads and greater depth than gene-level DE.

  • rnaseq.lncrna.librarystrongteam
    When question.goal = lncRNA
    Recommends
    • library.prep → rRNA_depletion
    • library.stranded → yes
    • sequencing.target_reads_per_sample → 50M
    Why does this matter?

    Many lncRNAs are not polyadenylated, are often antisense to coding genes, and are expressed at low levels. Use rRNA depletion (keeps non-polyadenylated RNA), a stranded library (resolves antisense transcripts) and deeper sequencing (~50M reads).

  • rnaseq.spikein.global_changestrongteam
    When question.expected_global_transcription_change = yes
    Recommends
    • library.spike_in → ERCC_per_cell_number
    Asks for
    • sample.cell_counts_available
    Why does this matter?

    Standard normalization assumes most genes are unchanged. If the perturbation may shift total transcription (e.g. degrons of global regulators, transcription inhibitors), add spike-ins proportional to cell number, not to RNA mass.

  • rnaseq.spikein.not_neededinfoteam
    When question.expected_global_transcription_change = no · question.goal = gene_level_de
    Recommends
    • library.spike_in → none
    Why does this matter?

    Spike-ins are not required for standard differential expression.

2

Samples

Organism, sample source, preservation, RNA quality (RIN, DV200), input amount, sex.

  • rnaseq.low_inputstrongteam
    When sample.input_ng < 10
    Recommends
    • library.prep → low_input_full_length
    • library.umi → yes
    Why does this matter?

    Very low input libraries have high duplication; use a low-input chemistry and UMIs.

  • rnaseq.pdx.host_readsstrongteam
    When sample.source = pdx
    Recommends
    • analysis.host_read_removal → yes
    Why does this matter?

    PDX tissue contains mouse stroma; plan computational removal of mouse reads (e.g. combined reference).

  • rnaseq.prep.degradedstrongteam
    When sample.preservation = ffpe
    Recommends
    • library.prep → rRNA_depletion
    Asks for
    • sample.dv200
    Why does this matter?

    FFPE RNA is fragmented; poly(A) capture loses 5' coverage. Use rRNA depletion and assess quality by DV200 rather than RIN.

  • rnaseq.prep.whole_blood_globinstrongteam
    When sample.source = whole_blood
    Recommends
    • library.globin_depletion → yes
    Asks for
    • sample.collection_tube
    Why does this matter?

    Globin transcripts can consume a large share of reads in whole blood, reducing effective depth for other genes.

  • rnaseq.quality.dv200_lowstrongconsultteam
    When sample.dv200 < 30
    Recommends
    • library.prep → rRNA_depletion
    Why does this matter?

    DV200 below 30% means most RNA fragments are shorter than 200 nt. Library yield and complexity are likely to be poor and many samples may fail. Discuss with the Bioinformatics team before committing samples (re-extraction, more input, or excluding samples). Threshold adopted by the team from library-kit vendor guidance; not an ENCODE standard.

  • core.sabv.both_sexessuggestteam
    When sample.sex = both
    Recommends
    • design.sex_balanced → yes
    Asks for
    • design.sex_balanced
    Why does this matter?

    Balance sex across conditions so sex is not confounded with treatment, and include sex as a covariate in the model. Testing sex differences themselves needs a larger design.

  • rnaseq.blood.edta_tubesuggestteam
    When sample.source = whole_blood · sample.collection_tube = edta
    Why does this matter?

    EDTA tubes do not stabilize RNA; transcript profiles change within hours at room temperature. Prefer RNA-stabilizing tubes (PAXgene, Tempus). If EDTA is unavoidable, standardize and record time-to-processing for every sample.

  • rnaseq.prep.intact_standardsuggestteam
    When sample.preservation ∈ {fresh_frozen, fresh} · question.goal = gene_level_de · sample.rin ≥ 7
    Recommends
    • library.prep → polyA
    Why does this matter?

    Intact RNA and a gene-level question: poly(A) selection is the standard, cost-effective choice.

  • rnaseq.quality.low_rinsuggestteam
    When sample.preservation ∈ {fresh_frozen, fresh} · sample.rin < 7
    Recommends
    • library.prep → rRNA_depletion
    Asks for
    • sample.dv200
    Why does this matter?

    RIN below 7 indicates partial degradation. Poly(A) capture then biases coverage toward the 3' end; rRNA depletion is more robust to degradation. Also measure DV200, which is more informative than RIN for degraded RNA.

  • core.animal.replicate_definitioninfoteam
    When sample.source ∈ {animal_tissue, pdx}
    Why does this matter?

    For animal studies, a biological replicate is an individual animal. Animals in one cage share environment, so spread conditions across cages and litters, and record cage and litter for the batch layout.

  • core.cell_line.replicate_definitioninfoteam
    When sample.source = cell_line
    Asks for
    • sample.passage_range
    • sample.str_authenticated
    • sample.mycoplasma_tested
    Why does this matter?

    For cell lines, biological replicates are independent cultures (separate passages or thaws, processed on different days), not wells split from one flask.

  • core.human_subjectsinfoteam
    When sample.organism = human · sample.source ∈ {patient_tissue, whole_blood, pbmc}
    Asks for
    • project.irb_status
    Why does this matter?

    Human subject material: confirm IRB status. Do not enter PHI in this tool.

  • core.organism.otherinfoconsultteam
    When sample.organism = other
    Why does this matter?

    Organisms without a well-annotated reference genome need a consult: alignment, annotation and possibly de novo transcript assembly must be planned before sequencing.

  • core.organoid.replicate_definitioninfoteam
    When sample.source = organoid
    Why does this matter?

    For organoids, independent lines from different donors are the strongest replicates. If only one line is used, replicates are independent passages cultured and treated separately, and conclusions apply to that line only.

  • core.sabv.askinfoliterature
    When sample.organism ∈ {human, mouse, rat}
    Asks for
    • sample.sex
    Why does this matter?

    NIH expects sex to be considered as a biological variable in vertebrate animal and human studies (NOT-OD-15-102), and reviewers assess it under Rigor. Record the sex of subjects, animals or cell lines; it is also a useful QC check (XIST / Y-chromosome genes).

  • core.sabv.single_sexinfoliterature
    When sample.organism ∈ {mouse, rat} · sample.sex ∈ {male, female}
    Why does this matter?

    Single-sex animal studies need a stated justification in NIH applications (NOT-OD-15-102), e.g. a sex-specific disease model. Note the justification in the design document.

  • core.sorted_cells.replicate_definitioninfoteam
    When sample.source = sorted_cells
    Asks for
    • sample.input_ng
    Why does this matter?

    For sorted cells, a biological replicate is an independent sort from a separate animal or donor, not a split of one sort. Record sorting purity and the number of cells per sample, which determines RNA input and library chemistry.

  • rnaseq.prep.pbmcinfoteam
    When sample.source = pbmc
    Recommends
    • library.globin_depletion → no
    Why does this matter?

    PBMCs generally do not need globin depletion; note any RBC contamination during isolation.

  • rnaseq.quality.dv200_moderateinfoteam
    When sample.dv200 ≥ 30 · sample.dv200 < 50
    Recommends
    • library.prep → rRNA_depletion
    Why does this matter?

    DV200 of 30-50% indicates moderately degraded RNA. rRNA depletion is appropriate; expect lower library complexity than intact RNA. Threshold adopted by the team from library-kit vendor guidance; not an ENCODE standard.

3

Library

Library prep, strandedness, globin depletion, spike-ins, UMIs.

  • rnaseq.prep.three_prime_tag_incompatibleblockteam
    When library.prep = three_prime_tag · question.goal ∈ {isoform, splicing, fusion, lncRNA}
    Why does this matter?

    3' tag libraries sequence only the 3' end of polyadenylated transcripts. They cannot resolve isoforms, splice junctions or fusions, and miss non-polyadenylated lncRNAs. Use a full-length library (poly(A) or rRNA depletion) for this question.

  • rnaseq.depth.gene_levelsuggestencode
    When question.goal = gene_level_de · library.prep ∈ {polyA, rRNA_depletion}
    Recommends
    • sequencing.target_reads_per_sample → 30M
    Why does this matter?

    ENCODE4 targets 30M aligned reads per replicate for bulk RNA-seq (20M in older projects). For DE, additional replicates add more power than depth beyond ~20-30M.

  • rnaseq.depth.three_prime_tagsuggestteam
    When library.prep = three_prime_tag
    Recommends
    • sequencing.target_reads_per_sample → 10M
    • sequencing.paired_end → no
    Why does this matter?

    3' tag libraries yield one read per transcript end, so gene-level counts saturate at lower depth than full-length libraries; about 10M reads per sample, single-end, is sufficient. Not an ENCODE standard (ENCODE does not cover 3' tag RNA-seq).

  • rnaseq.library.unstrandedsuggestteam
    When library.stranded = no
    Recommends
    • library.stranded → yes
    Why does this matter?

    An unstranded library cannot assign reads to the correct strand where genes overlap on opposite strands, which mis-assigns counts for a few percent of genes and rules out antisense analysis. Use unstranded only to match an existing unstranded dataset.

  • rnaseq.spikein.ercc_fractionsuggestencode
    When library.spike_in ∈ {ERCC, ERCC_per_cell_number}
    Recommends
    • library.spike_in_target_fraction → 0.02
    Why does this matter?

    ENCODE uses ERCC (Ambion) Mix 1 at about 2% of mapped reads. Too little gives noisy spike-in estimates; too much wastes sequencing depth on spike-ins.

  • rnaseq.library.stranded_defaultinfoteam
    When library.stranded not given
    Recommends
    • library.stranded → yes
    Why does this matter?

    Stranded libraries record which DNA strand each transcript came from. This resolves overlapping and antisense genes and is required to quantify antisense/lncRNA transcription. Stranded kits are now the default at most cores at little or no extra cost.

4

Design

Factors and groups, replicates per group, pairing, perturbation and controls.

  • core.replicates.noneblockteam
    When design.biological_replicates_per_group < 2
    Recommends
    • design.biological_replicates_per_group → 3
    Why does this matter?

    With one sample per group, biological variance cannot be estimated, so no statistical test of differential expression is valid and results cannot be called reproducible. This applies even to pilot studies.

  • core.replicates.minimumstrongteam
    When design.biological_replicates_per_group < 3
    Recommends
    • design.biological_replicates_per_group → 3
    Why does this matter?

    Differential testing needs at least 3 biological replicates per group to estimate biological variance. ENCODE's minimum of 2 targets reproducibility of reference data, not statistical power.

  • rnaseq.knockdown.controlstrongencode
    When design.perturbation_type ∈ {shRNA, siRNA, CRISPR_KO, CRISPRi}
    Recommends
    • design.matched_nontargeting_control → yes
    Why does this matter?

    ENCODE requires a matched control experiment for knockdown/CRISPR RNA-seq; include non-targeting controls.

  • core.design.paired_modelsuggestteam
    When design.paired = yes
    Asks for
    • design.pairing_factor
    Why does this matter?

    Paired design: include the pairing unit (patient, donor, litter) as a blocking term in the model, e.g. ~ patient + condition, and keep both samples of a pair in the same processing batch where possible. Losing one sample of a pair weakens the paired comparison.

  • core.design.pairing_questioninfoteam
    When sample.source ∈ {patient_tissue, whole_blood, pbmc, pdx} · design.paired not given
    Asks for
    • design.paired
    Why does this matter?

    Samples from the same patient, donor or PDX line (e.g. pre/post treatment, tumor/normal) are paired. Pairing removes between-individual variation from the comparison and changes both the analysis model and the power estimate, so it must be known up front.

  • rnaseq.knockdown.depth_floorinfoencode
    When design.perturbation_type ∈ {shRNA, siRNA, CRISPR_KO, CRISPRi}
    Why does this matter?

    ENCODE's floor for knockdown/CRISPR RNA-seq is 10M aligned reads per replicate. That is a QC minimum for detecting the targeted knockdown, not a target for genome-wide DE; the gene-level depth recommendation (30M) still applies.

  • rnaseq.prep.three_prime_tag_optioninfoteam
    When question.goal = gene_level_de · design.n_samples ≥ 96 · library.prep not given
    Why does this matter?

    With 96 or more samples and a gene-level question, a 3' tag-counting library is a cost-effective option: lower per-sample library cost and roughly 5-10M reads per sample. Trade-offs: no isoform information, and 3' bias makes it less suitable for degraded RNA from some sources. Discuss with the Bioinformatics team if budget is the constraint.

5

Batches

How samples are split across processing batches; condition must never be confounded with batch.

  • Seeded, balanced batch-layout generatorplanned
  • core.batch.confoundedblockteam
    When design.batch_confounded_with_condition = yes
    Why does this matter?

    Condition is fully confounded with processing batch; the effect of treatment cannot be separated from batch. Re-balance so each batch contains every condition.

6

Depth, read layout and length. Receives depth recommendations from earlier steps.
